feedback.problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 13 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(41{v}_{1}+37{v}_{2}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, since ${v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}41{v}_{1}+37{v}_{2} & =37{v}_{1}+4{v}_{1}+37{v}_{2} \\  & =37({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})+4{v}_{1} \\  & =37(0)+4{v}_{1} \\  & =4{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(41{v}_{1}+37{v}_{2})=T(4{v}_{1}).
$$

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(4{v}_{1}) & =4T({v}_{1}) \\  & =4[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 13 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-16 \\ 52 \\ -28\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(41{v}_{1}+37{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-16 \\ 52 \\ -28\end{aligned}].$
